title: Multiplayer FPS - WIP
author: Funny-Sprinkles-4518
selftext:
I've been working on improving the FPS game I started a few weeks back. I've added a few different maps, multiplayer, more weapons with sights and color schemes you can swap, smarter bots, and a bunch of little tweaks.

I am still doing everything with Claude Code. It seems like early on, Claude decided that I wanted everything THOROUGHLY commented. I have noticed that it takes a while for prompts to finish, and the amount of context used is fairly high (200k - 300k at the end of most). It runs through testing everything with Playwright and updates comments for anything it touched. So... iterating is a bit of a slow process, but it also seems like it usually doesn't make many mistakes. Maybe the amount of comments and testing that has become the repo's convention is slowing things down but preventing errors at the same time.

comments.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
comments.body:
what is your techstack fro client and server?

![gif](giphy|SVH9y2LQUVVCRcqD7o)

replies.author: Funny-Sprinkles-4518
replies.body:
The game is written in Typescript using Babylon.js and Havok for physics. The server is Node. It runs the same game simulation using Babylon's NullEngine, so when a client reports a hit, the server can rewind all of the targets to that point in time and check whether the ray was valid or not before recording it.

Thanks!

replies.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
replies.body: Nice my plan is the exactly the same but different languages. What do you use for communication between server and client?

replies.author: Funny-Sprinkles-4518
replies.body:
It uses websockets. That means it is over TCP at the moment. I have done a little bit of research, and it seems like UDP might be possible using webassembly if the overhead of TCP becomes an issue, but I decided not to spend time on it unless it becomes an issue.

The documentation on how multiplayer works is here if you want to look through it.

[https://github.com/idrum4316/hollowmere/blob/main/docs/multiplayer.md](https://github.com/idrum4316/hollowmere/blob/main/docs/multiplayer.md)

replies.author: HealthPuzzleheaded
replies.body: Thanks will take a look. I chose udp via webtransport. It was not easy to set up as you need to create a certificate and provide the client with the hash of it even for localhost and the cert is only 2 weeks valid so you cant just ship it with the client.

comments.author: Patient-Software-168
comments.body:
Can you give a guide on how you are doing?

Which engine, and so on

replies.author: Funny-Sprinkles-4518
replies.body:
Yeah. I'm using Babylon.js as the game engine, and Havok for physics. Havok is only used for ragdoll effects and breaking windows right now, but I am working on vehicles right now, and I am hoping I can use it to make buildings and things collapse under tank fire and stuff.

I considered porting it to a native engine like Godot before continuing with it, but I am honestly kind of curious how far I can go with Babylon. I decided that I don't plan to ever sell the game, so I went ahead and released the source code under the MIT license and kept going with it.

The server runs the same game loop using Babylon's NullEngine, and tracks the position of everyone. Shots that are reported as hits get rewound and verified server-side before they're recorded.

There aren't any 3d models. That decision was made after I created some character models and realized I was garbage at it. Claude's procedural models were better than the models I was trying to make, so I threw them out and went procedural for everything.

For maps, each map has a height map and a file that sets where each object is. I created a map editor where you can fly around, select objects, move them, rotate them, etc. And then Ctrl+S writes them back to the file so they can be committed. The map editor only works if you are running the dev server (\`npm run dev\`).

Let me know if there's anything else you want to know.

replies.author: Funny-Sprinkles-4518
replies.body:
You might be surprised at how much you can do and how quickly you learn.

If modifying an existing game seems less daunting than starting from scratch, you're welcome to clone mine and start trying to make changes or implement new features. The only thing you need to build and run it is Node.js.

[https://github.com/greywatch-game/greywatch](https://github.com/greywatch-game/greywatch) (I am in the process of renaming it because Hollowmere seems to be taken already)
